newsitem.title: GERMANY: German pension reform to pay for new tax cut-paper.
newsitem.headline: German pension reform to pay for new tax cut-paper.

text.p: Germany will try to partly offset a cut in the "solidarity tax" financing east German economic regeneration by carrying through with pension reform, the Handelsblatt business daily said.

In an advance summary of an article to appear on Thursday, Handelsblatt said senior coalition politicians had decided that the higher taxes firms will pay because of a planned lowering of pension contributions could finance the cut.
The lower contributions will in turn be financed by a one-percentage point increase in value-added tax to 16 percent, according to the newspaper.
Such a move would from next year mean increased income for federal and regional government of around three billion marks ($1.6 billion), the paper said, quoting Finance Ministry estimates.
Nobody was available at the ministry to comment.

The two-percentage point cut in the solidarity levy to 5.5 percent agreed to by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats earlier this week would cost the government some seven billion marks in revenue.
News of the solidarity cut sparked a row as east German politicians demanded that aid measures to the east do not suffer as a result.

The Handelsblatt also said Bonn planned to extend the time-frame for the collection of reserves intended to finance shutdowns of nuclear power plants from 19 to 25 years, a move that would bring in some two billion marks next year. ($ = 1.877 German Marks)
